tasks.title: FocusScope: a container's subtree takes keyboard events only while focused
tasks.description:
# What

Make the wrapper the host already puts around every mounted container the **keyboard gate**: pointer
events always enter; `Event::Key` and `Event::Widget` enter only while that container holds chrome
focus. This is what makes "the keys go to the focused component" implementable at all — without it the
host would have to know where each container sits in the retained tree.

# Current state

`FocusRing` (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/focus_ring.rs`, landed F003/P011/T020) wraps every container in
`focus_and_pick` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs`) and is bound to that mount's `keyboard_target` signal
(`SharedChromeState::container_keyboard_target`). It only **paints** — it does not gate anything.

`ScrollRegion::keyboard_target` (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/scroll_region.rs:476`) gates scroll intents
per region and stays useful for several scroll areas *inside* one container, but it is the wrong place
for the container-level gate (every future widget would need its own copy).

# The shape

The routing contract is in `heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs:682` (`dispatch`): `on_event_capture` first,
then the child walk unless `routes_own_subtree()`, then `on_event`. A gate that returns
`Handled::Yes` would stop the **sibling** walk, so the focused container would never be reached. The
expressible form is to own the walk:

```rust
fn routes_own_subtree(&self) -> bool { true }
fn on_event_capture(&mut self, ev: &Event) -> Handled {
    if matches!(ev, Event::Key { .. } | Event::Widget(..)) && !self.focused.get_untracked() {
        return Handled::No;              // not mine — my siblings still get their turn
    }
    route_event(&mut self.base.children, ev)
}
```

`route_event` is `pub(crate)`, which is another reason the gate belongs in the library beside the
wrapper rather than app-side.

# Steps

1. Add the gate to `FocusRing` (renaming it — `FocusScope`? — is a judgement call: the ring is the
   visible half of the same fact, so one widget with two jobs is honest, but the name should say
   scope). Update the rustdoc, `docs/widgets.md` and the showcase entry.
2. `tests/pointer_delivery.rs` **requires** anything claiming `routes_own_subtree` to still deliver
   every pointer kind (press/move/release/wheel) to its children — add the case, and make it pass for
   both focused and unfocused, because a click on an unfocused dock must still work (and should focus
   it: see the mouse task).
3. Tests: a widget intent reaches the focused scope's child and not an unfocused sibling's; an
   unfocused scope does not consume it (the sibling after it still gets it); pointer events enter
   regardless of focus.

# Acceptance

- One gate, in the library, beside the ring it shares a signal with.
- An unfocused container is inert to keys and fully alive to the mouse.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

---
**Completion summary:**
# ✅ DONE 2026-07-30 — commit `163f327`

`FocusRing` renamed to **`FocusScope`** (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/focus_scope.rs`) and given the
gate. The name says scope because the widget now has two jobs from one signal, and a reader seeing
"ring" would not expect it to swallow keys.

```rust
fn routes_own_subtree(&self) -> bool { true }
fn on_event_capture(&mut self, ev: &Event) -> Handled {
    if matches!(ev, Event::Key { .. } | Event::Widget(_)) && !self.focused.get_untracked() {
        return Handled::No;          // not mine — my siblings still get their turn
    }
    route_event(&mut self.base.children, ev)
}
```

**Why it has to own the walk**: swallowing (`Handled::Yes`) stops the walk at *this* node, so a
sibling scope — the one that actually holds focus — would never be reached; declining without owning
the walk would let the event through anyway, since `dispatch` does the child walk itself
(`component.rs:682`). So the scope takes the walk and skips it for the kinds that are not its own.
`Event::ModifiersChanged` is deliberately **not** gated (a broadcast; widgets keep modifier state
consistent either way).

## Tests

Six in `focus_scope.rs`: an intent enters a focused scope; does not enter an unfocused one; **an
unfocused scope declines so a focused sibling still gets its turn** (the load-bearing one — the inert
scope is placed *first*, which is the arrangement that breaks if it consumes); a key is gated like an
intent; every pointer kind reaches an unfocused scope; the gate follows the signal with no rebuild.

`tests/pointer_delivery.rs` gained two cases (focused + **unfocused**) requiring the whole pointer set
to reach the child — the unfocused one is the sharp case, since a click on a dock without focus is how
you focus it.

## Renamed everywhere

`heca-grid-ui/src/{lib.rs, widgets/mod.rs}`, `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs` (import, `focus_and_pick`, two
tests), `heca-renderer/examples/showcase.rs`, `docs/widgets.md` (section + TOC + focus-model table +
the ScrollRegion note), `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` §2.10, `AGENTS.md` catalog. `PaintCx::focus_ring`
(the paint primitive) keeps its name.

## Consequence for the next tasks

The gate is what P085/T352 dispatches into: the host sends one `Event::Widget(..)` at the chrome root
and only the focused container's subtree sees it. It also subsumes the container-level use of
`ScrollRegion::keyboard_target` — that setter stays useful for several scroll areas *inside* one
container, but the container-level gate is here now.

1017 tests, clippy clean.

tasks.title: Focus is the mode: route the keyboard to the focused component (absorbs the keyboard-scroll task)
tasks.description:
# What

Make chrome focus decide where unprefixed keys go. No `InputMode` variant: focus is already the fact,
and a mode beside it would be a second one that can disagree.

**This task absorbs CY8C2** ("ScrollRegion keyboard-scroll actions", canceled 2026-07-30 at the user's
request — they said the same thing). Everything CY8C2 still carried is transferred below, verbatim
where it is still true.

# Current state

`handle_keyboard_input` (`heca/src/app/input.rs:34`): `InputMode::Normal` forwards every unbound key to
the focused pane's backend (`:58-88`) after trying the `global` keymap. Prefix mode
(`handle_prefix_mode`, `:208`) resolves mode triggers, then the `normal` map, then **drops** the key
(`:275` — the `else if !ctx.key_text.is_empty()` arm just exits prefix). `InputMode::SidebarNav` is a
bespoke arm delegating to the `"sidebar"` mode keymap (`handle_sidebar_nav_mode`, `:584`).

# ✅ DECIDED — the order, in every focus state

1. prefix key → prefix mode → mode triggers → global `normal` map → **falls through to the focused
   component's `[keys.<kind>]` layer** (user decision 2026-07-29) → drop
2. global direct bindings (`Alt+Enter`, `Shift+PageUp`, …) — unchanged
3. **if a component holds chrome focus** → its layer → **swallow** if unbound (user decision: a `j`
   leaking into a shell is the worse failure)
4. otherwise → forward to the focused pane's backend, as today

`state.focused_pane` is **not** cleared: chrome focus redirects the keyboard, nothing else, so
`prefix+Enter` still splits the pane you last worked in.

# Steps

1. One branch at the top of the `InputMode::Normal` arm: chrome focus set ⇒ resolve in the component
   layer, else the existing terminal-forward path. Unbound ⇒ consume (do not forward).
2. Prefix fall-through: after the `normal` map misses, try the focused component's layer before
   dropping.
3. Suppress the **double-prefix literal forward** (`prefix_combo_to_literal_input`, `input.rs:224`)
   while a component has focus — nothing there is receiving text, so sending a literal `Ctrl+B` to a
   pane the user is not typing in is a surprise.
4. `Esc` returns focus to the pane (clear `focused_container`); `focus_dock` aimed at the
   already-focused dock toggles focus back off.
5. Status bar: derive the mode word from the focused component's `title()` (`status_mode_parts`,
   `app/render.rs:54`) so unprefixed keys never go somewhere invisible. The focus ring is the other
   half of that guardrail.

# Keyboard scrolling (was CY8C2)

## ✅ SHIPPED — the widget half (`096f06e`), unchanged by anything here

Eight `WidgetIntent` variants: `ScrollPageUp` / `ScrollPageDown` / `ScrollToTop` / `ScrollToBottom`
and the four horizontal ones. `ScrollRegion` acts on them:

- it owns the arithmetic — a page is 0.9 of its viewport, the edges clamp — because it is the only
  thing that knows its viewport and its content;
- it **declines** an axis it cannot scroll (axis off, or content fits), so a nested region or the host
  gets a turn; consuming would make the key silently do nothing;
- handled after the children, so the innermost scrollable region wins, as with the wheel;
- `keyboard_target(Signal<bool>)` gates which instance responds — per instance, position-agnostic,
  unset means yes. Bound to the mount's chrome focus by F003/P011/T020
  (`StateView::container_keyboard_target`).

**The logic lives in the widget, once.** Every `ScrollRegion` anywhere — any container, any nesting
depth, any region, any one added later — behaves identically with no per-usage code. That is the
standing requirement (user, 2026-07-28): *a widget holds its logic like a React component; move it
around the app and it works the same, without reinventing anything.* The host will only ever say
"one page down, this axis"; the widget decides everything else.

## ⚠️ THE ROUTE CHANGED — 2026-07-29, by the user. This supersedes the 2026-07-16/27 keys.

**Superseded:** vertical `prefix+Home/End/PageUp/PageDown`, horizontal `prefix+Shift+` the same four.
That shape existed only because there was no other way to stop the keys reaching the terminal.

**Now:** while a component holds chrome focus nothing is forwarded to a backend, so **plain
`PageUp` / `PageDown` / `Home` / `End` are free** and are the container's scroll keys; the existing
`Shift+` variants stay exactly as they are for the focused *pane*'s scrollback.

## The work

6. The bindings already exist and are already global/direct: `scroll_page_up = "Shift+PageUp"`,
   `scroll_page_down`, `scroll_to_top = "Shift+Home"`, `scroll_to_bottom = "Shift+End"`,
   `scroll_line_up/down` (`keybindings.default.toml`), handled today against the focused terminal
   viewport. **One branch at the top of those existing handlers**: chrome focus set ⇒ dispatch the
   matching `Event::Widget(WidgetIntent::Scroll*)` into the chrome tree — the FocusScope (P085/T351)
   delivers it to the focused container and every other container is inert — else the terminal
   viewport path, unchanged. One binding, one meaning: *scroll whatever has focus*.
7. **The four horizontal actions** still need adding (`ScrollPageLeft/Right`,
   `ScrollToLeftEdge/RightEdge` — the widget intents exist, no `WmAction` does), through the full
   Adding-New-Actions checklist (AGENTS.md): variant → `action_from_name` → `action_priority` →
   `action_policy()` → handler → `build_registry` → `keybindings.default.toml` → `ActionRegistry::ALL`
   descriptor **with its `args` declaration** → `rpc.rs` → README. Reuse `ResizeAxis`
   (`heca/src/input.rs:40`, `EnumArg::VALUES = ["x","horizontal","width","y","vertical","height"]`) if
   an axis argument is preferred over four names — optional, defaulting to vertical, so a plain binding
   stays legal (a *required* argument would forbid a bare key, F003/P010/T006).
8. A **declined** intent (`Handled::No` — e.g. a container with nothing scrollable) stops at the
   chrome; it does **not** fall through to the pane. The innermost-wins rule is about nested *scroll
   areas*, and the pane is not an outer scroll area of the sidebar.

## Still ruled out (2026-07-28, checked in code — do not re-open)

Feeding these through the **widget keymap** (`build_widget_keymap`, `heca/src/app/registry.rs:202`,
the `[keys.widgets]` config table that `Input`/`Select`/`Tabs`/`Dialog` use). It is consulted at
`heca/src/app/events.rs:156` inside a branch that requires **a modal to be open** and the mode *not* to
be `Prefix`/`HintPick` — so `[keys.widgets]` reaches focused widgets **inside modals only**. Do not add
a widget-keymap path beside the actions: it would be a second way to do one thing.

## The 2026-07-17 blocker is discharged

"No chrome surface mounts a `ScrollRegion`" is false since 2026-07-26: containers nest their own
(`heca/src/providers/workspaces.rs`). `GridKey` still has no `PageUp`/`PageDown` — and does not need
it, because the intent is semantic. That is the point of not delivering a key.

# Edge cases

- Prefix, hint pick, and every mode trigger must keep working while a component is focused (they are
  resolved first, by construction).
- A pick mode (`DockPick`, `PaneSelect`, …) is entered *from* a focused component and must still
  resolve normally.
- Nothing may reach a backend while chrome focus is set — audit every `process_input` call on the
  Normal path.

# Acceptance

- With a dock focused: its keys work unprefixed, `prefix+…` still works, unbound keys do nothing, and
  nothing reaches the terminal.
- Plain `PageUp`/`PageDown`/`Home`/`End` scroll the focused dock; the same keys with `Shift` still
  scroll the focused pane when no dock is focused. Every other scroll area declines.
- Horizontal scrolling reachable from RPC through the same actions, one code path.
- No second mechanism for the same job.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings. **The USER drives it in the app** — this is interaction,
  with more than one scroll area on screen (P085(F007)/T359 seats the second one).

tasks.title: Provider gains kind(), actions() and perform() — a component declares what only it can do
tasks.description:
# What

The trait every component that wants actions adheres to. It declares **only** what nothing else can do
(selection-dependent semantics); everything else it wants is an existing action it *binds*.

# ✅ DECIDED — `perform`, not one closure per action (user, 2026-07-29)

```rust
fn kind(&self) -> &str;                      // the TYPE — config namespace `[keys.docker]`
fn actions(&self) -> Vec<ActionMeta>;        // declaration only; empty is a real answer
fn perform(&self, id: &str, args: &Intent, cx: &mut ProviderCx<'_>) -> Handled;
```

Why `perform` over `Vec<(ActionMeta, DynHandler)>`:

- **It is the shape a WASM component is forced into** — an id + args crosses the boundary, a closure
  does not. Native and plugin stay one design.
- `&self` is available (the host is calling *into* the component); a closure outlives `actions()` and
  must hoist every piece of state it needs into `Rc`s at registration.
- `DynHandler` is `Fn(&mut AppState, …)` — **full mutable app state**, which §2.3 forbids a provider.
  `ProviderCx` (read + emit) enforces the contract in the type instead of by discipline.
- "Which instance?" is answered once, by the host, rather than captured per closure.

The closure form stays for the **host's own** dynamic actions (the chrome placement ones), which
legitimately take `&mut AppState`.

# Current state

- `Provider` (`heca/src/providers/mod.rs:35`): id, supported_regions, default_region, default_order,
  title, movable, grow, collapsible, keyboard_navigable, build_contribution, context_menus,
  on_activate. No kind, no actions.
- `register_dynamic` (`heca/src/actions.rs:409`) + `ActionMeta` (`:2063`, carrying an unused
  `default_binding`) + `ActionHandle` + `unregister_dynamic` all exist and are exercised by tests only.
- `ProviderHandles` (`providers/mod.rs:100`) is documented as where the unregister handles join.
- `WorkspacesContainerProvider::placed(id, region)` (`providers/workspaces.rs:69`) makes `id()` the
  **mount** id — there is no `kind()`, so two placements look like two unrelated components.

# Steps

1. `Provider::kind() -> &str`, defaulting to `id()` for the single-placement case; workspaces returns
   `"workspaces"`. Bindings and declared actions key off `kind()`; cursor/scroll/focus key off `id()`.
2. `ProviderActions` (or the same trait) with `actions()` + `perform()`. Default `actions() = vec![]`
   so a container that declares nothing compiles and behaves — that is the one-number-widget case.
3. `ProviderCx<'_>`: the **mount id**, the shared store (an `Rc` alias — no borrow of `AppState`
   held), `selected() -> Option<&str>` (this mount's cursor row), `state()` (the read-only
   `StateView`), `dispatch(name, args)` / `emit(intent)` queued and drained by the host after
   `perform` returns.
4. The host bridge, written **once** for every component that will ever exist:
   ```rust
   fn route_to_owner(state: &mut AppState, intent: &Intent) {
       let Some(mount) = owning_mount(state, &intent.action) else { return };
       let store = state.chrome_state.clone();
       let mut cx = ProviderCx::new(&mount, store, state.intent_sink());
       if let Some(p) = state.chrome_host.provider(&mount) { p.perform(&intent.action, intent, &mut cx); }
       cx.drain_into(state);
   }
   ```
   Borrow note: the provider lives *inside* `state.chrome_host`, so no `&mut AppState` may be alive
   during `perform` — `ProviderCx` holds only clones and a queue.
5. `owning_mount`: the focused mount if it owns the id, else the **last-focused instance of that kind**,
   else the first mounted. Written down once, not decided per call site.
6. Register on mount / retire on unmount: `on_activate` returns the declared metas in
   `ProviderHandles`; the **host** calls `register_dynamic` (a provider never mutates app state) and
   `unregister_dynamic` on unmount.
7. `ActionMeta.default_binding` stops being dead code — consumed by the config task.

# Edge cases

- Re-registering the same id on remount replaces the previous entry (already the documented behaviour).
- Two placements of one kind share declared actions and bindings; `perform` is called on the placement
  `owning_mount` picked, and reads *its* cursor.
- `perform` returning `Handled::No` (nothing selected) is a legitimate silent decline; a later
  `can_perform` could grey out a menu entry — do NOT build it now.

# Acceptance

- A component declares two actions and a five-line `perform`, and gets keys, RPC, palette, context menu
  and the confirm gate from that alone.
- No component can reach `&mut AppState`.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

---
**Completion summary:**
Provider gained kind(), actions() and perform() — the contract by which a component declares what only it can do. Present and in use: heca/src/providers/mod.rs:64 (kind), :187 (actions, returning Vec<ActionMeta>), :233 (perform), with a test provider implementing the same three at :500/:516. The decided shape was ONE perform(name, args) rather than a closure per action, and a component declares only selection-dependent semantics — everything else it wants is an existing action it binds. ProviderCx carries the mount id, the shared store as an Rc alias (no &mut AppState held), selected(), state() and queued dispatch/emit drained by the host after perform returns. The host bridge is written once for every component.

**Verification:**
Shipped and in use — the trait and its call sites are live in heca/src/providers/mod.rs and the workspaces container was migrated onto it by T356. NOT verified by me in this session: I am closing the evidence gap the planner flagged, not re-testing the work. It was driven by Antonio when it landed.

**Remaining or unverified:**
None for this task. But note that P035(F003)/T506 now questions the shape of the READ half this contract leans on: ProviderCx::state() returns StateView, whose 20 hand-written selectors a plugin cannot extend.

**Files touched:**
- heca/src/providers/mod.rs
- heca/src/actions.rs
- heca/src/chrome/
decisions: perform(name, args) — one entry point, not one closure per action.
A component declares ONLY what nothing else can do; everything else is an existing action it binds.
ProviderCx holds an Rc alias of the store, never &mut AppState, because the provider lives inside it.

tasks.title: nav_key: a row declares its identity once — cursor, right-click target, later drag
tasks.description:
# What

One declaration on a row, three readers. A component labels its rows; the host derives the keyboard
cursor, the context-menu `(path, target)`, and (later) the drag identity from it. No app-side enum of
row kinds anywhere.

# Current state — three closed enums doing this job

- **Right-click**: `mouse.rs` hit-tests the sidebar into a `ChromeDragItem`
  (`Pane | Column | Workspace` — a closed domain enum) and `open_sidebar_context_menu`
  (`heca/src/mouse.rs:143`) **matches on it** to produce `(ContextPath, ContextTarget)`. `ContextTarget`
  is closed too (`Pane / SidebarPane / SidebarColumn / SidebarWorkspace`). A plugin row cannot be
  expressed, so a `container.docker` path could never be produced — the contribution is filtered out
  and the menu is empty.
- **Keyboard menu**: `resolve_active_context` (`chrome/context_menu.rs:308`) reads
  `InputMode::SidebarNav` + the sidebar cursor — a second, keyboard-specific resolution of the same
  fact.
- **Cursor**: `SidebarTree.cursor` + `WorkspacesContainerState.nav_selection`, re-projected after every
  rebuild by `apply_nav_selection` — correct in shape (identity, not an index) but domain-typed.

The precedent to copy is the hint registry: rows already register *the intent a click fires*
(`hints.register(InteractionIntent::FocusPane { pane_id })`, `providers/workspaces.rs:201`) and
`collect_hint_targets` (`heca-grid-ui/src/hint.rs:45`) walks a subtree in document order.

# Steps

1. **Library**: `Base.nav_key: Option<…>` + a builder (`.nav_key("abc")`), and a collector that walks a
   subtree in document order returning `(nav_key, bounds)` — the hint collector's twin (or the same
   walk, extended). Rustdoc + `docs/widgets.md`.
2. **Cursor, per mount**: `container_cursor: HashMap<mount, Option<NavKey>>` in `SharedChromeState`,
   beside `container_scroll` and `focused_container`. Survives a tree rebuild because it is an identity,
   not an index — this is why a scoped `FocusManager` (a `usize` visit index, `heca-grid-ui/src/focus.rs:50`)
   cannot be the cursor.
3. **Highlight**: generalise `ChromeSignals.pane_nav`/`ws_nav` (domain-keyed today) to
   `(mount, NavKey, Signal<bool>)`, driven from the cursor in `sync_chrome_signals`. `Row`/`Item`/
   `DockFrame`/`MarkerGroup` already expose `nav_state()`.
4. **Scroll-into-view**: a cursor row overrides `wants_visible()` (`component.rs:543` — documented for
   exactly "a list's navigation cursor"), so the enclosing `ScrollRegion` follows it with nothing wired.
5. **Right-click resolution moves to the tree**: walk the retained chrome tree at the cursor,
   innermost-first (as `drag::resolve_at` and `collect_hint_targets` already do), take the first node
   carrying a `nav_key`, and produce `path = container.<kind>` (derived from the owning component) +
   `ContextTarget::Row { container: mount, key }`. An optional per-row `.context_path(..)` override
   covers a component with several row kinds in one body.
6. **`ContextTarget` gains the open `Row` variant** and `row_key()`. The closed variants stay until the
   workspaces migration (next task) removes them.
7. **`resolve_active_context` stops naming SidebarNav**: the focused container + its cursor produce the
   same `(path, target)` the pointer path produces. `prefix+>` and right-click then resolve identically
   for every component.

# Edge cases

- Two placements of one component: cursors are per mount (this is the T021 lesson — scroll offsets
  keyed by kind made two placements move together, invisible until there were two).
- A rebuild between the cursor being set and read: re-project by key; a key that no longer exists clears
  the cursor rather than pointing at a neighbour.
- Rows that are not navigable simply carry no `nav_key`.

# Acceptance

- One declaration per row; the cursor, the context menu and the keyboard menu all read it.
- No `ChromeDragItem` match in the context-menu path.
- A plugin row can be right-clicked and its component's entries appear.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

tasks.title: Per-kind keybindings: a component's bindings, merged by key, live only while it is focused
tasks.description:
# What

Per-component keymaps: shipped defaults, user-overridable one key at a time, resolved only while that
component holds chrome focus.

# Current state

- The keymap is built from config **at load** (`build_keymap`, `heca/src/app/registry.rs`), before any
  provider activates — so a declared `ActionMeta.default_binding` (`actions.rs:2072`,
  `#[allow(dead_code)]`) reaches nothing today.
- Config merge rules (AGENTS § Config Loading): tables merge **per key**; scalars and **arrays are
  replaced wholesale**. That is why `[[keys.mode]]` blocks have to be merged back by name at runtime
  (`build_modes`) — a user redefining one mode would otherwise lose the built-ins.
- `action_ref_from_config(name, args)` already resolves a name to `ActionRef::Builtin` **or**
  `ActionRef::Dynamic` at press, so binding a component's own id needs no new resolution.
- `[keys.unbind]` already removes a binding **by key combo**, "whatever it points at".

# ✅ DECIDED — the shape

```toml
[keys.docker]                 # a TABLE: merges per key, so overriding one keeps the rest
restart_selected = "r"        # the component's own action (its kind namespaces it)
stop_selected    = "s"
focus_next_pane  = "n"        # ← an EXISTING built-in, just bound here

[[keys.docker.bind]]          # the arg-carrying form — arrays are otherwise replaced wholesale,
action = "spawn_command"      #   so these merge by their `keys` field (a keymap IS a map from
keys   = "t"                  #   combo to action; merging on the combo is not a special case)
args   = { command = "lazydocker", float = "true" }

[keys.docker.unbind]          # explicit removal — NOT null/empty-string semantics (the program
"s" = true                    #   catalog uses `disabled = true` for the same reason)
```

# Steps

1. Parse `[keys.<kind>]` (table), `[[keys.<kind>.bind]]` (array, merged by `keys`) and
   `[keys.<kind>.unbind]` in `heca-config` beside the existing `[keys]`/`[[keys.mode]]` handling.
2. Merge-by-key for the array form: a user entry with the same `keys` replaces the default's; everything
   else survives. This is the fix that makes the arg-carrying form usable at all.
3. **Bind declared defaults at mount** (`bind_component_default`): after a provider's actions are
   registered, bind each `ActionMeta.default_binding` into that kind's layer **unless the user already
   bound that key or rebound that action id** — user config always wins, and a default never silently
   shadows one.
4. Resolution: while a component holds chrome focus, its layer is consulted (see the routing task).
   Built-in components ship their defaults in `keybindings.default.toml` so the defaults stay
   discoverable (AGENTS: a default that lives only in code is a bug); a **plugin** has no line in that
   file, so its manifest is the source there, with user config still winning.
5. Document both in `README.md` and `keybindings.default.toml`, including the merge-by-key rule and
   `unbind`.

# Edge cases

- A binding to an id whose component is not mounted is **not** an error (config is read before
  providers register — the existing `ActionRef::Dynamic` rule): it simply does nothing until the
  component appears.
- Two placements of one kind share the layer (bindings belong to the type; only state is per mount).
- A component that declares no actions and binds nothing needs no table at all.

# Acceptance

- `[keys.docker] stop_selected = "x"` changes one key and keeps `r` and `t`.
- `[[keys.docker.bind]]` with `keys = "t"` replaces exactly that default and keeps the others.
- `ActionMeta.default_binding` is no longer dead code.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.

tasks.title: Migrate the workspaces container onto the contract; delete SidebarNav and the sidebar_* built-ins
tasks.description:
# What

Make the first-party container the first consumer of the contract, and remove the bespoke mode it
replaces. This is the task that proves the design: if the workspace tree cannot be expressed as a
component that declares its actions, the design is wrong.

# ✅ SETTLED — THE SIDEBAR TREE **IS** THE COMPONENT (user, 2026-07-30)

Re-stated because a session asked it again and the task text did not answer it. **Do not re-open.**

- **A component declares its actions** (→ `ActionRegistry`) **and their default keybindings**
  (→ the keymap registry, user-configurable). That is the whole of its contract.
- **It is up to the component to perform an action against its own focused item.** For
  `WorkspacesContainerProvider` that item is a workspace, a column or a pane — *it* knows which,
  because those are its rows.
- **`SidebarTree` is that component's own domain state** — the analogue of `DockerService` in the
  worked example. It lives on `AppState` today for historical reasons only.
- **Therefore cursor movement is a DECLARED COMPONENT ACTION**, not a host facility. There is no
  generic host-side "step to the next `nav_key`": a component like a hypothetical
  *CurrentSelectedWorkspace* label declares **no** actions at all — it only reads state — and a
  host-defined notion of "next row" would be meaningless to it.
- `nav_key` (landed, F003/P085/T354) keeps its host-side job: **naming** a row so the cursor
  highlight, the right-click target and later the drag can point at one. *Which* row is next is the
  component's.
- A component that declares nothing can still get a **context menu**: its entries may name existing
  actions or its own.

`ProviderCx::set_selected` (landed, F003/P085/T353) is how a component moves its own cursor — it
writes the per-mount cursor in the **store**, never `&mut AppState`.

# ⚠️ THE PREREQUISITE THE TASK DID NOT DECLARE (found 2026-07-30)

**Where the tree goes: `WorkspacesContainerState`** (`heca/src/chrome/state.rs:142`), *not* a field
on the provider struct. The reason is concrete: a provider is stored as `Box<dyn Provider>`, so
anything app-side that wanted the tree back would need `as_any` + a downcast — host code reaching
into one specific component, which is the thing the pluggable design exists to prevent.
`WorkspacesContainerState` already **is** this component's own state (`nav_selection`,
`collapsed_ws`, `panes`, `selection`), it is already reachable from `ProviderCx::state().workspaces()`
with no downcast, and F003/P085/T360 already plans to key it by container. Put the tree there.

**But it cannot move yet**, because the app still reads `AppState.sidebar_tree` at **46 sites across
10 files**, and the biggest group is a *legacy fixed-row geometry* path that is still live:

- `heca/src/sidebar/hit_test.rs` — `sidebar_hit_test` / `sidebar_button_hit_test`, row resolution by
  arithmetic on row height;
- `heca/src/mouse/surface_left.rs` (7 sites) and `heca/src/mouse/drag.rs` (3) — reached from
  `mouse.rs:331` via `target::surface_click_action`, so it is **not** dead code;
- `heca/src/chrome/mod.rs` — `pane_fallback_name` / `pane_custom_name` lookups, and the
  `state.sidebar_tree.workspaces` walk at `:3644`.

`nav_key` was built precisely to replace that: `nav::nav_key_at` resolves the topmost-deepest row
under a point from the **retained** tree's real laid-out bounds, the same walk `drag::resolve_at`
uses. So **step 0 of this task is to delete the fixed-row path** and re-source the name lookups from
the store, after which the tree has one owner and one home.

Order that keeps the build green:

0. Replace `sidebar_hit_test` / `sidebar_button_hit_test` with `nav_key_at` + the existing
   `drag::resolve_at`; delete `heca/src/sidebar/hit_test.rs` and the `flat_items` / `button_hitboxes`
   readers. Re-source `pane_fallback_name` / `pane_custom_name` from `WorkspacesContainerState`.
1. Move `SidebarTree` into `WorkspacesContainerState`; delete `AppState.sidebar_tree`.
2. Declare the actions + `perform`.
3. Ship `[keys.workspaces]` defaults.
4. Context menu → `container.workspaces` + `ContextTarget::Row`.
5. Delete `SidebarNav` + the 11 `sidebar_*` built-ins.
6. Docs + tests.

# What is being deleted

- `InputMode::SidebarNav` (`heca/src/app_state.rs:58`) + `handle_sidebar_nav_mode`
  (`heca/src/app/input.rs`) + `restorable_mode` (`chrome/context_menu.rs:334`, whose only arm is
  `SidebarNav`).
- The 11 `sidebar_*` built-ins: `sidebar_focus`, `sidebar_up`, `sidebar_down`, `sidebar_left_nav`,
  `sidebar_right_nav`, `sidebar_peek`, `sidebar_expand_toggle`, `sidebar_create_workspace`,
  `sidebar_create_column`, `sidebar_split_in_column`, `sidebar_zoom_selected_column`,
  `sidebar_delete_selected` — their `WmAction` variants, `action_from_name` arms, `action_priority`
  arms, handlers (`handlers.rs:1562+`), registrations (`app/registry.rs`), descriptors, RPC commands
  and the `[[keys.mode]] name = "sidebar"` block. **~140 references.**
- The legacy fixed-row hit-testing above.
- `state.chrome_state.workspaces.nav_selection` → the generic `container_cursor`, and with it the
  single bridge `publish_sidebar_selection` → `selection_nav_key` that F003/P085/T354 left behind
  **precisely so there is one place to delete here**.

# What replaces it

`WorkspacesContainerProvider` declares:

- `kind() = "workspaces"` (bindings) vs `id()` = the mount (cursor, scroll, focus). **Landed** in
  F003/P085/T353.
- **Declared actions**, each acting on its own focused item: `workspaces.cursor_up` /
  `workspaces.cursor_down`, `workspaces.activate_selected` (focus the pane/workspace under the
  cursor — today's `sidebar_right_nav`/Enter), `workspaces.peek_selected` (focus but stay),
  `workspaces.toggle_selected`, `workspaces.rename_selected`, `workspaces.delete_selected`,
  `workspaces.create_workspace`, `workspaces.create_column`, `workspaces.split_selected`,
  `workspaces.zoom_selected`. Each with label, icon, `policy`, and `confirm` where destructive.
- **Bindings it does not declare**: anything already in the catalog (`zoom_column`, `close`,
  `next_pane`) is simply **bound** in `[keys.workspaces]`, not redeclared.
- `perform` resolves the cursor (`cx.selected()`) against its own tree and dispatches the existing
  parameterized actions (`FocusPane`, `RenamePaneById`, `DeleteWorkspace`, …) through `cx.dispatch`.
- Defaults shipped as `[keys.workspaces]` in `keybindings.default.toml`, preserving today's letters
  (`j`/`k`/`h`/`l`/`Enter`/`Space`/`Tab`/`w`/`c`/`v`/`z`/`d`) so muscle memory survives.

`sidebar_focus` (`prefix+e`) becomes: focus the navigable dock (already implemented, F003/P011/T020) —
the mode it used to enter no longer exists, because focus **is** the mode.

# Behaviours to preserve (settled with /grill-me; do not casually re-decide)

Navigation is selection-driven; the cursor does not move main focus; `h`/`l` are tree navigation on
structural rows; `Enter`/`l`/`Right` activate **and leave**, `Space` peeks **and stays**; `Esc` exits
and focuses contextual content; mutation keys are container-only; the global collapse actions act on
the **active main-view** state, not the cursor.

# Acceptance

- `prefix+Shift+e` → pick the dock → `j`/`k`/`Enter`/`d` work, unprefixed, exactly as `prefix+e` used to.
- No `SidebarNav`, no `sidebar_*` action, no domain enum in the menu/nav path, no fixed-row geometry.
- A component that declares **no** actions still works and can still carry a context menu.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings. **The USER drives it in the app.**

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE — commit `7cc63b1`. Verified by the user in the app on 2026-07-29 across several rounds. 1063 tests, clippy 0 warnings.

STEP 3 — the mutations are on the contract
`heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs` declares `create_column` (`c`), `create_pane` (`p`), `delete_selected` (`x`), `delete_selected_column` (`Shift+x`), `zoom_selected` (`z`), keyed in `keybindings.default.toml` under `[[keys.component]] name = "workspaces"`. Each resolves the cursor to a target and dispatches an EXISTING parameterized action; none reimplements anything. `WorkspaceTree::locate_pane` was added so the component answers "which column is this pane in" **from its own model** — the handlers it replaced asked the session, which a component cannot reach.

**`zoom_column_at_index { ws_idx, col_idx }` is new** (user's design call): `zoom_column` takes no args, so there was nothing to dispatch. `delete_column` was already indexed and is reused rather than renamed — an existing id used by the context menu — with its description corrected from "the focused column" to "the named column".

**"New workspace" is deliberately NOT declared.** It is about no row, so it is not the component's; `w` binds the built-in `create_workspace`. It also could not have worked: a short name matching a built-in resolves to the built-in, by design. That dropped the old handler's floating-pane guard, which the user accepted as incidental.

**The startup report caught a real defect**: `delete_column = "Shift+x"` bound the *built-in*, which needs args a key cannot supply — "will do nothing when pressed". Renamed to `workspaces.delete_selected_column`.

**Policies are per action, not per component.** The cursor six are `Global` (chrome state, drivable while a pane floats); the five mutations are `TiledOnly`, as the `sidebar_*` built-ins they replace were. A shared default in the `act()` closure had silently made all eleven `Global` — a real widening, caught by the user asking about ActionPolicy.

STEP 5 — the deletion
The twelve `sidebar_*` actions and everything naming them; `[[keys.mode]] name = "sidebar"`; `InteractionIntent::EnterSidebarNav`; the `publish_sidebar_selection` → `selection_nav_key` bridge; the twelve `sidebar-*` RPC commands.

`prefix+e` is now `global_focus` on the component. `focus_dock` **reveals the region it focuses** — `handle_sidebar_focus` did this and nothing else did. Taking chrome focus became `TiledOnly` (releasing stays `Global`): the old `Global` was justified as "unlike `SidebarFocus`, which enters a nav mode that moves pane focus", and that stopped being true. The user hit exactly this — driving the dock over an open float with nothing happening.

The five overflow fallbacks in the pane pickers now call `focus_navigable_dock` instead of `sidebar_focus`. **Explicitly a stopgap**: the app still knows a navigable dock exists. It deletes itself when the pickers take component-provided targets (F003/P086/T365 / T367).

The dock cursor now follows the active pane (`heca/src/app/focus.rs`, in `sync_focus`), writing both `nav_selection` (what the tree re-derives its positional cursor from) and the per-mount `container_cursor` (what the row outlines draw). Chosen by the user over the narrower alternatives.

DELIBERATELY LEFT: `InputMode::SidebarNav`'s husk
Nothing enters it. Not deleted here because `resolve_context_for` reads it to decide which menu `prefix+>` opens, and the replacement signal is container focus — **F003/P086/T365's design work**, written up in full on that task along with the resulting live regression (`prefix+>` opens the pane's menu, not the cursor row's; the mouse path is unaffected) and the settled rule that **a container's context menu is always provided by the component itself**.

A CAPABILITY REMOVED WITHOUT REPLACEMENT
The twelve `sidebar-*` RPC commands. `parse_rpc_command` returns a `WmAction`, a closed enum, so it structurally cannot express a component's declared action. That affects every component and plugin action, not just these. Acknowledged by the user; needs its own task.

tasks.title: Hooks: what is focused, what is selected, what was dispatched
tasks.description:
# What
Let a component or plugin observe focus, row selection and accepted action dispatch through the shared chrome event bus, without polling or reading AppState. Subscribers observe and queue intents; they do not veto dispatch.

# Current state and ownership
- Focus already emits ChromeEvent::ContainerFocusChanged.
- Row selection already emits ChromeEvent::ContainerCursorChanged { container, key } from SharedChromeState::set_container_cursor, with a change guard. Reuse this event. Do not introduce a second ContainerSelectionChanged event for the same change. SidebarSelectionChanged is not present in the reviewed main sources; do not plan its deletion as new work.
- T357 owns event coverage and the missing ActionDispatched notification. T360 owns per-mount values and ViewNode bindings. P035(F003)/T506 owns public namespace reads. No new StateView selectors belong here.

# Steps
1. Verify the existing focus and cursor events cover the public observation contract, including two placements of the same component. Keep one event path for row selection.
2. Emit ChromeEvent::ActionDispatched { name, args, source } once at the accepted dispatch point, after policy and required confirmation/argument checks allow execution and before execution. Cover built-in and component actions through the shared dispatch path; canceled or refused actions must not be reported as executed. The notification itself does not prove successful completion.
3. Keep event payloads usable by the planned plugin bridge without handing subscribers AppState or private execution objects. Reuse existing serializable action data.
4. Subscribers observe; a follow-up action is queued rather than synchronously dispatched inside the event callback. Document and test re-entrancy behavior. No veto API.
5. Document the existing focus/cursor notifications and new action notification in docs/chrome-and-ui.md. Public readable state is supplied by T506, not by adding container_selection(mount) to StateView.

# Current source locations
- heca/src/chrome/state/events.rs: ChromeEvent and its stable names.
- heca/src/chrome/state/shell.rs: SharedChromeState focus/cursor setters.
- heca/src/app/interaction/dispatch.rs, route.rs and view_intent.rs: accepted action paths, policy and component action dispatch.

# Verify
Subscribers see focus, selection and accepted dispatch without AppState. Existing selection events are reused, duplicate notifications are absent, unchanged values emit nothing, refused/canceled actions emit no dispatch notification, and queued follow-ups cannot re-enter the same dispatch synchronously.
Run ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test and ./scripts/lint-changed.sh. Use scoped checks, never a whole-workspace run. No code was implemented or verified by this planner correction.

checklist.title: Reuse ContainerFocusChanged and ContainerCursorChanged as the single focus/selection event path; do not add a duplicate selection event.
Emit ActionDispatched once for accepted built-in and component actions, after policy/confirmation/argument checks and before execution.
Document the three notifications and observe-only / queued follow-up rule in docs/chrome-and-ui.md.
Test subscribers observe focus, selection and accepted dispatch without AppState, including independent mount identities.
Test unchanged focus/cursor values and one accepted action do not emit duplicate notifications.
Test blocked, invalid or canceled actions emit no ActionDispatched notification.
Test queued subscriber follow-ups and re-entrancy behavior; run the scoped test and Clippy gates.

tasks.title: Palette and RPC reach a component's actions from anywhere: FocusContainerThenAction
tasks.description:
# What

A declared action must be usable without first focusing its component by hand — from the command
palette, from RPC, from a menu — while still meaning something (a selection-dependent action needs its
component to be the focused one).

# ✅ DECIDED (user question 2026-07-29: "what will the command palette discover?")

**Everything registered, and registration follows mounting.** A component's actions enter the catalog
on mount and are retired with it (`ProviderHandles` + `unregister_dynamic`), so an action for a
component that is not mounted simply does not exist — no filtering needed, it falls out.

**Mounted but unfocused: still shown.** Choosing one focuses its component and then performs, using the
precedent already in the codebase for exactly this problem: pane-header buttons whose action needs the
pane focused register `InteractionIntent::FocusPaneThenAction { pane_id, action }`, which
`dispatch_intent` expands into focus-then-act (`heca/src/app/interaction.rs`, and see AGENTS §
"Active-targeted buttons must focus first").

# Steps

1. `InteractionIntent::FocusContainerThenAction { container, action }`, expanded in `dispatch_intent`
   into `FocusDock { dock } ` + the action — mirroring `FocusPaneThenAction` exactly.
2. Palette entries for component actions carry it, and are labelled with their scope:
   `"Containers › Restart Container"` — the component's `title()` + the action's `label`, both already
   in metadata. The focused component's actions sort first; nothing is hidden.
3. **Which instance**, when a kind is mounted twice: the last-focused instance of that kind, else the
   first mounted. One rule, written down once (`owning_mount`, shared with the `perform` bridge) rather
   than decided per call site.
4. RPC: the same resolution, plus an explicit override for scripts — `--dock docker.right` — so a script
   can target a specific placement without focusing it first.
5. `list-actions` / `describe-action` include component actions with their owner, so introspection shows
   who owns what.

# Edge cases

- A selection-dependent action chosen from the palette with nothing selected: `perform` declines
  silently after focusing. Acceptable for now; a later optional `can_perform(&self, id) -> bool` would

tasks.title: A component's own signals: a per-mount value store a plugin can write
tasks.description:
# What
Give a component a place to keep **state the retained UI tree binds to**, keyed by mount, that a WASM plugin can write across the boundary. Today a plugin's only way to show a changed value is to re-send its whole `ViewNode` tree.

# Two kinds of state — only one is a gap
- **Component's own domain state** (Docker client, container list, poll timer) lives **in the component** — native provider holds a struct field; WASM plugin owns its linear memory. Host not involved.
- **State the retained tree binds to** is the gap. The tree lives host-side and a `ViewNode` is static serializable data that **cannot carry a signal** (AGENTS.md ⭐ SETTLED). Native container flips a `Signal` and its `Label` repaints in place; a plugin can only re-send the tree. This closes that asymmetry.

# What already exists — the pattern, twice
`SharedChromeState` already holds lazily-created, mount-keyed cursor and scroll signals in `heca/src/chrome/state/shell.rs`. Do not assume the older `container_keyboard_target` map still exists. The existing per-mount cursor and scroll maps share the properties this needs — created on first ask, keyed by mount id, outlive the retained tree, change-guarded setter emits `ChromeEvent`.

# Steps
1. Add to `SharedChromeState` beside the two above:
   ```rust
   container_values: Rc<RefCell<HashMap<(String, String), Signal<PropValue>>>>, // (mount, key)
   ```
2. Read/create and write accessors on `SharedChromeState`, following the existing per-mount store pattern. Creation receives an explicit default (the previously proposed `container_value_or`); an ordinary read must not invent a value. `PropValue` has no `Null` and must not grow one. Agree the public builder syntax before implementing it; the map/accessor sketch describes the store, not a registry API plugin authors must assemble.
3. One event: `ChromeEvent::ContainerValueChanged { container: String, key: String }` (`heca/src/chrome/state/events.rs`), plus its `name()` arm — `"container.value.changed"`. Carry the key, not the value; subscribers read through the signal.
4. **Exposure is via the namespace facade (T506)** — not `StateView`. When T506 lands, the facade serves the namespace by `kind()`. This task does **not** add accessors to `StateView`.
5. Write side goes on `ProviderCx` (built by F003/P085/T353) so §2.3 holds — a provider never gets `&mut AppState`.
6. `ViewNode` binding: a `bindings` map on the node, beside `events` (decided 2026-08-04 by Antonio):
   ```rust
   struct ViewNode {
       kind, props,
       events:   Map<EventName, Intent>,   // already exists
       bindings: Map<PropName, String>,    // prop name → value key
       children,
   }
   ```
   Precedence: read literal from `props`, then **let a binding override it** by looking up `container_value(mount, key)` and binding the widget's signal. `.text("Running").bind("text", "daemon_status")` reads as what it is.
7. `WorkspacesContainerState` (`heca/src/chrome/state/workspaces.rs`, held by `shell.rs`) — hardcoded field for the one built-in container. T359 is still planned and must not be described as already completed. Verify actual placements when this task starts. Fold it into the same keyed registry, or explicitly justify why it stays privileged — but do not leave the comment describing a future that has arrived.

# Edge cases
- Two placements of one container: independent values, same as scroll and focus. Test with two mount ids writing the same key → two answers.
- Lifetime: values die with the mount, like dynamic-action handles in `ProviderHandles` (`providers/mod.rs:100`). An unmounted container must not leak its map entries.
- Rebuild of the retained tree must not reset a value — the signal lives in the store.
- Setter stays change-guarded, or a plugin polling once a frame emits an event per frame.

# Acceptance
- A provider can create, read and write a named value keyed by its mount, with no host code that knows the key.
- A `ViewNode`-described widget bound to a value updates **without a tree rebuild**.
- `WorkspacesContainerState` is either keyed by container or explicitly justified as privileged.
- Run ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test and ./scripts/lint-changed.sh. Antonio drives the plugin case in the app: a value changing on screen with no rebuild is a visual check, not proof supplied by a unit test.
# Ownership and integration
T360 implements the value store, change notification, write path and declarative widget bindings once. T357 supplies focus/selection/dispatch notifications; T506 consumes the store through the public read-only namespace facade and must not reimplement these parts. Keep values and cursor/scroll state scoped by mount; component domain data may remain shared where that is intentional. Record the WorkspacesContainerState decision with evidence.

# Current source locations
heca/src/chrome/state/{shell,workspaces,events}.rs; heca/src/providers/mod.rs; heca-view/src/node.rs (ViewNode data); heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs (the single realization bridge). Preserve ViewNode as serializable data; host-side realization binds signals. No implementation or verification is claimed by this planner correction.

tasks.title: REGRESSION: dragging a pane in the sidebar stopped working; dragging a column still works
tasks.description:
# The bug

Reported by the user in the app, 2026-07-29, after this session's commits. **Dragging a pane card in
the sidebar does nothing. Dragging a column still works.** It worked before the session.

Confirmed still broken after `866f7da` (the `.both()` scroll-axis revert), so the second scroll axis
is **not** the cause.

# What is already ruled out

- **A widget swallowing the press.** That would break column drag too. It does not.
- **The pane card's drag declaration.** `git diff 163f327..HEAD` on
  `heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs` shows no change to `.draggable(drag_id)`,
  `.drop_target(drag_id)` or `drag.register(ChromeDragItem::Pane(..))`. The card still declares
  itself exactly as before.
- **The four deleted surface functions** (`contains`, `item_at`, `can_accept`, `update_hover` in
  `heca/src/mouse/surface_left.rs`, plus their dispatchers in `target.rs`). Their dispatchers carried
  `#[expect(dead_code)]`, which clippy verifies is *fulfilled* — so they were provably unreachable
  before deletion. Look here last.

# Where to look, in order

1. **`drag::source_at` resolution** (`heca-grid-ui/src/drag/resolve.rs:105`). It walks children
   last-added-first and descends before testing the parent, so the deepest drag source under the
   point wins. A pane card sits **inside** the column's `MarkerGroup`, and both are drag sources. If
   the pane is no longer reached, the column answers instead — which is exactly the symptom. What is
   new on that path is `.nav_key(..)` on both (`bfa8296`), and the `FocusScope`/`KeyHint` wrappers
   from earlier phases. Check `skip()` in that file: it skips a subtree whose `visible` is false or
   whose `style.layout.hidden` is set.
2. **`heca/src/mouse.rs:272-278`** — `chrome_dispatch_press` returns early when a widget consumed the
   press, *before* `sidebar_drag_source` is called at `:278`. A `Row` has `on_activate` and consumes;
   a `MarkerGroup` does not. That asymmetry matches the symptom exactly. This ordering pre-dates the
   session, so if it is the cause, something else changed what the `Row` does with a press.
3. **`heca/src/mouse/drag.rs:92`** — `handle_sidebar_drag_starting` reads the workspaces model, which
   moved into a `RefCell` in `51d7874` (`state.chrome_state.workspaces.tree()`). A borrow held across
   a call that reaches back into the store panics; a borrow taken and dropped is fine. Verify the
   drag-label build there is not silently failing.

# How to reproduce and bisect

The session's commits, oldest first: `3bfe4f6`, `69b4158`, `bfa8296`, `51d7874`, `898ca40`,
`a71d737`, `aa73bbe`, `050f1f9`, `866f7da`. `git bisect` against "drag a pane card in the left
sidebar" will name the commit in three or four steps; `bfa8296` (retained-tree row resolution) and
`51d7874` (the model move) are the two that touched this area.

# Acceptance

- Dragging a pane card in the sidebar moves/reorders it as it did before the session.
- Dragging a column still works.
- A regression test that fails without the fix — `drag::source_at` over a built tree with a pane
  inside a column is unit-testable in `heca-grid-ui` without a window.
- **The USER drives it in the app** — this is a pointer gesture; no unit test verifies it end to end.

---
**Completion summary:**
REGRESSION fixed: dragging a pane card in the sidebar had stopped working while dragging a column still worked — reported by Antonio in the running app on 2026-07-29, after that session's commits, and confirmed still broken at 866f7da. The pane card is both a drag source and a drop target and carries its own opaque DragItemId; that wiring is live at heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs:78.

**Verification:**
Reported by Antonio in the app and closed on his re-test — the only way a drag regression can be verified, since a green suite had it passing while it was broken. NOT re-verified by me in this session.

**Remaining or unverified:**
None.

**Files touched:**
- heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs
- heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs
decisions: A row's drag identity comes from its nav_key (T354), so the cursor, the right-click target and the drag id cannot drift apart — which is what made this class of regression possible before.
